name: Joseph of Arimathea
whenBasis: The crucifixion under Pilate (AD 26–36), dated to the Passover of AD 30 or 33 by reckonings from the weekday the gospels give.
summary: A rich man from Arimathea, a respected member of the council who had not consented to its decision, and who was waiting for the kingdom of God; John says he was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, for fear of the Jews. On the evening of the crucifixion he went boldly to Pilate and asked for the body. With Nicodemus he wrapped it in linen with spices and laid it in his own new tomb cut in the rock, and rolled a stone across the entrance.
body: Pilate is surprised Jesus is already dead and checks with the centurion before giving him the body. The women from Galilee watch where it is laid.

later.text: Medieval English legend, first written down in the thirteenth century, brings him to Glastonbury with the Holy Grail.

sources.title: The Grail: From Celtic Myth to Christian Symbol
sources.author: Roger Sherman Loomis
